source.title: Rehearsal revealed: The limits and merits of revisiting samples in continual learning
source.authors: Eli Verwimp; Matthias De Lange; T. Tuytelaars

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports how additional rehearsal-memory updates affect generalization in continual learning, a setting not covered by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study tests rehearsal in continual learning, not the listed iid natural-label versus random-label claim or any of its specific versions. Its rehearsal-memory overfitting and loss-landscape findings are relevant to generalization but do not test a listed version. Table 1 reports average accuracy for ER and ER-step; the other cited methods and findings are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study tests rehearsal dynamics and memory overfitting in continual learning, which do not measure any listed version. Its loss paths and gradient norms do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. Random-label memorization is cited as motivation, not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that rehearsal tends to retain solutions within the first task's low-loss region, while overfitting combined with movement toward poorly approximated high-loss ridges harms generalization. Overfitting alone is insufficient to explain the harm. Their memory-only update heuristic improves reported mean accuracy, using the best positive update count from a grid search.
record.recipe_differences: Continual-learning rehearsal experiments with sequential task distributions and limited exemplar memories; not the iid random-label memorization/generalization setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ER-step gains vary with dataset and rehearsal memory size; the authors state gains are larger for smaller memories and decline on the more difficult CIFAR10 and Mini-Imagenet sequences.

fits_no_version.finding: The selected ER-step configurations have higher mean evaluation accuracy than ER in every Table 1 comparison, with gains ranging from 0.1 to 9.4 percentage points. Update counts were selected by grid search; significance is not established for every comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional memory-only updates can improve continual-learning evaluation accuracy under the tested rehearsal recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss-path and gradient-norm analyses indicate that rehearsal solutions remain connected to the first-task solution while memory loss can remain low as first-task test loss rises. Appendix A reports little memory overfitting after two CIFAR10 tasks, with stronger overfitting after five.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rehearsal-memory fit can diverge from retained-task generalization as a continual-learning sequence progresses.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The experiments concern class-incremental continual learning rather than iid training and testing. Accuracy results are averaged over five initializations; the study reports no random-label control. Loss-landscape evidence is partly figure-based, with some additional plots in the appendix.
record.rows_left_out: No reported Table 1 rows were omitted. Other figures report loss paths and gradient norms, but their plotted values are not specified numerically in the text and do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Matched random-label and natural-label training, fitting capacity, and held-out accuracy relative to chance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on matched image tasks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout versus a matched control. Selecting dropout from two positive rates does not establish its effect relative to no dropout.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with train-test gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with other generalization measures.
Influence-defined memorized-example removal versus equal-sized random removal followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification with discusses/T6. A new setting qualifies as T3 only when its results bear on a listed version. Table 1 values are accurately transcribed, but these method-performance rows belong under fits_no_version rather than as claim-test evidence. Table 2 adds MNIST method comparisons outside all versions, so it does not require a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels under standard training.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and their held-out performance.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
